relevance_reason: Reports 3 unrelated patients with de novo heterozygous ATP5MC3 missense variants causing dystonia and/or spasticity with functional ATPase studies, and summarizes the ATP5MC3-associated phenotype together with the previously reported multigenerational family.

findings.statement: Zech et al. (2022) described 3 unrelated patients with de novo heterozygous ATP5MC3 missense variants. Patient 8, a previously reported 12-year-old boy, had isolated upper-limb dystonia. Patient 9, a 15-year-old girl, had a history of milestone delay, pyramidal signs, and generalized dystonia with prominent upper-body involvement. Patient 10, a 6-year-old boy, had delayed psychomotor development, lower-extremity spasticity, and elevated blood lactate.
quotes: The first individual (patient 8), heterozygous for c.318C>G (p.Asn106Lys), was a previously reported 12-year-old boy who manifested isolated upper-limb dystonia.
this 15-year-old girl had a history of milestone delay, pyramidal signs, and generalized dystonia with prominent upper-body involvement
this 6-year-old boy displayed delayed psychomotor development, lower-extremity spasticity, and elevated blood lactate levels

findings.statement: In a 12-year-old boy with isolated upper-limb dystonia (patient 8), identified from a cohort of 1,012 dystonia patients with whole-exome sequencing, Zech et al. (2022) found a de novo heterozygous c.318C>G (p.Asn106Lys) variant in ATP5MC3, the same variant previously identified in an independent pedigree with 18 of 40 members affected by dystonia and/or spasticity. The variant was absent from gnomAD and local control exomes. Patient fibroblasts showed a slight but significant decrease in ATPase activity and reduced oxygen consumption rate.
quotes: Additional molecular features of c.318C>G (p.Asn106Lys), identified in patient 8 and in an independent pedigree with 18 of 40 related members affected by dystonia and/or spasticity, have been described recently.

we also studied this individual`s newly established fibroblast cultures and found that c.318C>G (p.Asn106Lys) produced a slight, but significant decrease in ATPase activity in this subject (Figure 5e). Additionally, patient 8’s OCR was reduced
The de-novo variants were not reported in either gnomAD or local control-exome databases.

findings.statement: In a 15-year-old girl (patient 9) with milestone delay, pyramidal signs, and generalized dystonia, Zech et al. (2022) identified a de novo heterozygous c.319C>G (p.Pro107Ala) variant in ATP5MC3 by whole-exome sequencing. The variant was absent from gnomAD and local control exomes, affected a stringently conserved residue near the FO-F1 interaction loop, and was predicted deleterious by in silico tools.
quotes: A c.319C>G (p.Pro107Ala) variant was found in the second individual (patient 9)
Asn106 and Pro107 are localized at the FO-F1-subcomplex interaction site, suggesting that mutations involving these invariant positions may translate into compromised ATPase function.

findings.statement: In a 6-year-old boy (patient 10) with delayed psychomotor development, lower-extremity spasticity, and elevated blood lactate, Zech et al. (2022) identified a de novo heterozygous c.236G>T (p.Gly79Val) variant in ATP5MC3, absent from gnomAD. Patient fibroblasts showed deficient ATPase activity and a moderate decrease in assembled ATPase on BN-PAGE; modeling placed Gly79 at an interhelical contact site possibly interfering with c-ring integrity.
quotes: The third individual (patient 10) had the variant c.236G>T (p.Gly79Val)

enzyme assays performed on patient 10`s fibroblasts identified a deficient ATPase activity (Figure 5e); this enzymatic defect was associated with a moderate decrease in assembled ATPase, as demonstrated by BN-PAGE (Figure 5f).

findings.statement: Combining their 3 ATP5MC3 patients with the multigenerational family reported by Neilson et al., Zech et al. (2022) found that the ATP5MC3-associated condition included dystonia (12/18), spasticity/pyramidal signs (17/18), and developmental delay/intellectual disability (2/18). Dystonia-predominant syndromes were seen in 10 individuals; the authors noted that patients 9 and 10 confirmed spastic symptoms in independent families and introduced neurodevelopmental comorbidity.
quotes: features of the ATP5MC3-associated condition include dystonia (12/18), spasticity/pyramidal signs (17/18), and developmental delay/intellectual disability (2/18).

Notably, our description of the previously unreported patients 9 and 10 confirms the manifestation of spastic symptoms in independent families with ATP5MC3 variants, and newly introduces the expression of neurodevelopmental comorbidity.

findings.statement: Zech et al. (2022) found that ATP5MC3 c.236G>T, associated with a more severe neurodevelopmental disease-spasticity presentation, produced a significantly greater ATPase enzyme deficit than c.318C>G, associated with isolated dystonia, although they cautioned that further studies were required before genotype-phenotype correlations could be postulated.
quotes: our experiments performed for patients 8 and 10 revealed that ATP5MC3 c.236G>T, associated with a more severe neurodevelopmental disease-spasticity presentation, produced a significantly greater ATPase enzyme deficit than ATP5MC3 c.318C>G, associated with isolated dystonia.

findings.statement: Zech et al. (2022) suggested that dominant-negative effects could underlie disease caused by ATP5MC3 (and ATP5F1A) variants, supported by mild-to-moderate ATPase assembly and/or enzyme-activity defects in several patient cell lines.
quotes: Dominant-negative effects could well be possible, as supported by the observation of mild-to-moderate ATPase assembly and/or enzyme-activity defects in several patient lines.

relevance_reason: Identifies the ATP5MC3 p.Asn106Lys variant as the cause of autosomal dominant early-onset dystonia and/or spastic paraplegia in a large family and in a de novo case, with functional studies in patient cells and Drosophila.

findings.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) summarized a large, multigenerational family (Family-1) segregating autosomal dominant dystonia and/or spastic paraplegia. Of 40 individuals in the pedigree, 18 were affected with either childhood-onset, progressive generalized dystonia or adult-onset, gradually progressive spastic paraplegia. Less severe, later-onset focal limb and neck dystonia and spasmodic dysphonia also occurred. Brain MRI and peripheral nerve physiology were normal when performed.
quotes: The autosomal dominant pedigree included 40 individuals, of which 18 were affected with either childhood-onset, progressive generalized dystonia or adult-onset, gradually progressive spastic paraplegia.

Less severe, later-onset, focal limb and neck dystonia and spasmodic dysphonia also occurred, possibly related to trauma or overuse. Brain MRIs and peripheral nerve physiology, when performed, were normal.

findings.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) reported that the Family-1 proband had unilateral upper limb dystonia onset at age 2 years that generalized to the trunk and all limbs, causing loss of ambulation. His father and grandfather had the hereditary spastic paraplegia phenotype, with progressive leg weakness and spasticity beginning after age 20 years. Metabolic studies, including blood lactate and pyruvate, serum amino acids, urine organic acids, and acylcarnitine profiles, were normal in the proband and his father.
quotes: the proband had unilateral upper limb onset at age 2 years that generalized to trunk and all limbs, resulting in loss of ambulation.
The proband’s father and grandfather manifest the HSP phenotype with onset of progressive leg weakness and spasticity after age 20 years.
Metabolic studies, including whole blood lactate and pyruvate, serum amino acids, urine organic acids, and acylcarnitine profiles from blood and urine were normal in both the proband and his father.

findings.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) reported that bilateral pallidal deep brain stimulation, implanted at age 9 years in the Family-1 proband, restored ambulation and limb use, and the response remained excellent at age 25 years.
quotes: Bilateral pallidal deep brain stimulation, implanted at age 9 years, restored ambulation and limb use. At age 25 years, his response remains excellent.

findings.statement: In affected members of Family-1, a family whose disorder had previously been mapped to chromosome 2q24-q31, Neilson et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing restricted to the linkage region to identify a heterozygous missense variant in the ATP5MC3 gene (c.318C>G, p.Asn106Lys). Sanger sequencing showed that only affected individuals carried the variant. The variant was absent from gnomAD v2.1.1 and v3.1.1, affects a highly conserved loop that contacts the F1 subunit, and was predicted damaging by all in silico tools used. The authors concluded that ATP5MC3 remains the primary candidate for the spastic paraplegia in this family.
quotes: Exome analysis revealed a variant (c.318C > G; p.Asn106Lys) (NM_001689.4) in ATP5MC3 in a large family with autosomal dominant spastic paraplegia and dystonia that cosegregated with affected individuals.
Consistent with the pedigree phenotypes, Sanger sequencing showed only affected individuals carrying the ATP5MC3 variant.
The p.Asn106Lys variant has not been documented in gnomAD v2.1.1 or v3.1.1.

findings.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) described a right-handed boy (Family-2) of European descent, born to healthy unrelated parents with no family history of movement disorders. He presented at age 11 years with a 4-year history of gradually worsening upper limb dystonia. Blood, urine, and CSF studies and a dystonia gene panel were unrevealing, and brain MRI showed nonspecific mild bilateral frontoparietal white matter changes.
quotes: who first presented to the Department of pediatric neurology in Freiburg (Germany) at the age of 11 years with a 4-year history of gradually worsening upper limb dystonia.
Brain MRI revealed nonspecific mild frontoparietal white-matter changes bilaterally without other associated abnormalities.

findings.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) used parent-offspring trio whole-exome sequencing in the Family-2 proband and found the same heterozygous ATP5MC3 c.318C>G (p.Asn106Lys) variant, which had arisen de novo. GeneMatcher had identified this match. The authors stated that this result confirmed the variant's pathogenicity for dystonia.
quotes: parent-offspring trio WES revealed a NM_001689.4:c.318C>G (p.Asn106Lys) variant as a heterozygous, de novo mutation in the proband
The pathogenicity of this variant for dystonia has been confirmed by the identification of the same variant in a patient with upper limb dystonia from a second, independent family.

findings.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) screened 384 patients (362 with dystonia and 22 with hereditary spastic paraplegia) for variants in ATP5MC1, ATP5MC2, and ATP5MC3 and found no deleterious variants.
quotes: Samples from patients with dystonia (n=362) and HSP (n=22)
No deleterious variants were identified in the cohort of patients with dystonia or spastic paraplegia (Supplementary Table 1).

findings.statement: In fibroblasts from the Family-1 proband (dystonia) and his affected father (HSP), Neilson et al. (2022) found normal activities of complexes I through IV. Complex V activity was reduced by 20%, cellular ATP by 20 to 32%, and oxygen consumption by 21 to 25%. Because oxygen consumption and ATP were reduced in proportion, the authors did not consider uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation a likely mechanism.
quotes: activities of electron transport chain complexes I through IV were equivalent to controls. However, Complex V activity was reduced by 20% (p < 0.01) (Figure 2). Similarly, cellular ATP was reduced 20% to 32% and oxygen consumption 21% to 25% (Figure 2).
Uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation, however, was not supported as a mechanism for the human mutation, as both oxygen consumption and ATP were proportionally reduced.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial ATP synthase complex

findings.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) noted that ATP5MC1 and ATP5MC2 also encode subunit c, so haploinsufficiency of ATP5MC3 would be unlikely to explain the severe phenotypes. They hypothesized that the mutant protein interferes with the F1-F0 interaction. They also suggested that differences in the relative expression of the mutant gene, for example between striatum and spinal cord, may account for the variable phenotype.
quotes: Assuming equal expression of the three alleles, haploinsufficiency would be unlikely to account for the severe phenotypes, as 83% of the active protein would still remain. Thus, we hypothesized that the presence of the mutant allele interfered with the F1-F0 interaction which could be tested through overexpression.
Thus, we suspect that relative expression of the mutated gene may mediate phenotypic expression.

findings.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) overexpressed the Drosophila ATP5MC3 ortholog (CG1746) carrying either the human-equivalent p.N102K or the E. coli-equivalent p.N102E mutation under the arm-GAL4 driver. Both mutant lines climbed less well than wildtype in geotaxis assays, with p.N102K the slowest, whereas overexpression of wildtype protein had no effect. In fly mitochondria, complex V activity was reduced by 53% with p.N102K and by 37% with p.N102E.
quotes: At less than one week of age, the human disease mutant subunit c (p.N102K) and the equivalent bacterial mutation (p.N102E) demonstrated reduced mobility relative to wild type flies and the arm-GAL4; UAS-WT construct
the Complex V activity was reduced by 53% for the human p.N102K mutant (p=0.0008) and by 37% for the bacterial p.N102E mutant (p=0.003)

findings.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) reported that dystonia in Family-1 showed incomplete penetrance. Childhood-onset dystonia could generalize, and the spastic paraplegia began in adulthood and progressed gradually without other neurological problems.
quotes: Dystonia in this pedigree can generalize if manifest in childhood, shows incomplete penetrance, and responds to pallidal deep brain stimulation. The spastic paraplegia presents in adulthood, progresses gradually, and is not accompanied by other neurological problems.

relevance_reason: Reports the original large Ohio kindred with autosomal dominant spastic paraplegia and dystonia, and maps the locus to 2q24-q31.

findings.statement: Gilbert et al. (2009) reported a large multigenerational Ohio kindred with a highly penetrant autosomal dominant neurologic disorder causing spasticity and dystonia. Spasticity and weakness began anywhere from the first year of life to the sixth decade, and dystonia began between the first and third decades. Affected members had no ataxia and no apparent cognitive involvement. Neuroimaging and peripheral neurophysiology were normal.
quotes: We report clinical and genetic data from large Ohio kindred with autosomal dominant (AD) HSP and DYT.
Age of onset of spasticity and weakness is from the first year to the sixth decade, and age of onset of DYT from the first to third decade.
There is no ataxia or apparent cognitive involvement. Neuroimaging and peripheral neurophysiology are normal.

findings.statement: Gilbert et al. (2009) reported that generalized dystonia improved markedly with deep brain stimulation in 1 affected child from the kindred.
quotes: Generalized DYT improved markedly with deep brain stimulation in 1 child.

findings.statement: Gilbert et al. (2009) used single-point and multipoint linkage analysis with microsatellite markers and SNP array genotyping to map the disease locus in the Ohio kindred to chromosome 2q24-q31. The region was flanked by rs1424937 and rs1559510, lay proximal to SPG13, and contained no known HSP or dystonia genes. A secondary analysis looking for candidate regions segregating with the dystonia phenotype found two regions with parametric lod scores above 2.0.
quotes: The disease locus was mapped to a region on chromosome 2q 24-31, flanked by markers rs1424937-rs1559510, proximal to SPG13, in a region where there are no known HSP or DYT genes.
A secondary analysis for candidate genes segregating with the DYT phenotype revealed two candidate regions with parametric lod scores above 2.0.

findings.statement: Based on the clinical presentation and the linkage results, Gilbert et al. (2009) concluded that this disease is a novel neurologic disorder, distinct from known forms of hereditary spastic paraplegia and dystonia.
quotes: On the basis of clinical presentation and linkage results, we conclude that this disease is a novel neurological disorder.
